text.p: British Gas Plc, demerged earlier this month, on Thursday posted a sharp drop in 1996 profits.
The company said its historical cost profit on a pre-exceptional basis was 631 million pounds ($1 billion) for 1996 compared to 903 million pounds a year earlier.
British Gas said its financial performance in 1996 benefited from colder weather but was hit by continuing weak prices in industrial and commercial markets, as well as restructuring costs.
Exceptional charges for the year totalled 1.14 billion pounds ($1.9 billion).
The company, which hived off its gas supply business into a new firm called Centrica, said that group had a proforma loss of 1.06 billion pounds last year.
BG Plc, the company composed of the rest of British Gas, had a proforma profit of 381 million pounds last year.
BG Plc also proposed a final dividend of 8.1 pence per share, for a total of 14.5 pence for the year.
